questions.question:
**Direction: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'no error' as your answer.**

She have / left by the time / I reach home.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"She have". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"By the time"** is a temporal expression indicating when the first action (her leaving) will be completed.
 
• It establishes a point in time before which the action will be finished.
 
• There are two structure that are related to the phrase "By the time". 
 
 
• **Structure 1: By the time I reach the station, (Simple Present) the train will have left. (Future Perfect)**
 
• **Structure 2: By the time I reached the station (Simple Past), the train had left. (Past Perfect)**
 
 
 
• As per the structure 1** "She will have left" **uses the future perfect tense.
 
• The future perfect tense is formed by combining "will have" with the past participle of the verb.
 
• In this case, the verb is "left," which is the past participle of "leave."
 
• The future perfect tense is used to express an action that will be completed before another action in the future.
 
• And **"I reach home"** is in the simple present tense and indicates the second action, which is reaching home.
 
• The use of **"I reach home" **suggests a point in the future when the speaker will arrive home.
 
• Putting it all together, the sentence conveys that the action of "her leaving" will be completed before the speaker reaches home in the future.
 
• The future perfect tense is appropriate in this context because it emphasizes the completion of the action before a specified point in the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3". **

Therefore, the correct answer is:** *She will have left by the time I reach home*.**
